query: Explain how `run_simple` in `src/werkzeug/serving.py` starts the development server: how it validates its arguments, how it wraps the application for static files and for the debugger, how it picks the kind of server to build through `make_server`, and how it behaves differently when the reloader is enabled or when it is itself running inside the reloader.

operations.name: The port must be an integer
expressions: raise TypeError("port must be an integer")

operations.name: Static file mappings wrap the application in shared-data middleware
The debugger wraps the application and trusts the chosen hostname
A threaded and a multi-process server cannot be combined
expressions: raise ValueError("Cannot have a multi-thread and multi-process server.")

operations.name: The server class is threaded, forking or plain depending on the arguments

dependencies.name: A process running inside the reloader reuses the listening socket handed down through an environment variable, and the parent publishes it
Whether the process is a reloader child is decided from an environment variable
The startup banner is logged only in the original process, not in a reloaded child
With the reloader on the server runs under it and is always closed; otherwise it simply serves forever
